reviewType: Read-only static source and primary documentation review; not a penetration test or runtime pass
conclusion: No concrete privilege escalation, untrusted metadata shell injection or artifact path traversal was established in reviewed workflow source.

artifactBoundaries.sameRunReader: ios-prototype visual-review downloads one named current-run compact artifact; fixed categories/capture names, UUID-like PNG basename regex, unique path, symlink/containment checks, 1 MiB per image and 8 MiB total output.
artifactBoundaries.crossRunReader: review-xctest-evidence validates an 8 KiB request, run ID integer, 40-hex revision, artifact/capture allowlists; checks run repository and head SHA and one nonexpired artifact with matching workflow_run head SHA; paths constrained by basename regex, uniqueness, symlink and root containment checks; manifest 512 KiB, PNG 1 MiB/TXT 256 KiB, total 8 MiB.
artifactBoundaries.limits: Artifact metadata and downloaded content are transported as evidence, never executed. No privileged follow-on workflow. Cross-run source workflow ID and run attempt are not separately enforced; current policy selects explicit run ID and source SHA. No concrete spoofing route shown.

residuals: Actions use moving major-version tags; XcodeGen can be obtained from Homebrew without a repository lock. These are trust/reproducibility boundaries, not a demonstrated compromise.
Actual repository Actions settings, organizational policy and runner image integrity were not audited.

GitHub documents automatic artifact digest validation as warning on mismatch; emitted content SHA-256 values and printed archive metadata should not alone be called an independently verified archive. No observed digest mismatch.

Same-run visual reader does not impose a manifest size bound before read_text; artifact producers already execute at the same read-only workflow trust level, so no new privilege boundary breach was demonstrated.
